# Changelog

This file is no longer updated. Its entries end with commit `07f21da` (Continue runs within the request budget). Later changes, and earlier ones not listed below, are recorded in the commit history: each commit's subject and body state what changed, and a `Kogen-Intent: <slug>` trailer names the change's full description in `.kogen/intents/<slug>/intent.md`. List them with `git log`.

## v0.1.0 (unreleased)

- bbf3fdd Extract the standalone Kogen Loop
- b782019 Verify provider affinity and tool-batch replay
- 84c427d Add caller-owned shell duration bounds (later removed, see below)
- f47ec9f Restore timeout custody liveness
- 0665b58 Explain invalid Anthropic stream outcomes
- 2ea31bf Retry transient provider stream faults
- 3fd0443 Sweep command groups and refuse foreign kills
- 9c079e1 Store a token for the external executor
- bd627aa Keep the provider's bounded refusal message
- c7e8331 Fix two Linux test flakes
- Remove the unused `provider.Request.AnthropicCacheTTL` and `Budget`, `loop.Direct.Policy` (with `ContextPolicy`), `loop.Round.StopAfterTerminal` and `loop.SessionConfig.CacheID` options
- Remove the unused experimental levers: provider prefix-event logging (`provider.Client.PrefixLog`, `EndPrefixLog`, `PrefixEvent`), the read ledger (`loop.Round.ReadLedger`, `ReadLedger`, `NewReadLedger`, `Continuation`), terminal reminders (`loop.Round.TerminalReminders`, `loop.SessionConfig.TerminalReminders`, `loop.Hooks.TerminalReminder`, the `round.terminal_reminder` event), compact tool descriptions (`tools.Tools.CompactDescriptions`) and `tools.Tools.OmitViewImage`. Behavior is fixed at the former defaults: a response without a tool call ends the round, tool descriptions are full and `view_image` is offered whenever it is enabled. No default request, result, definition or tool-output bytes change.
- Remove the optional loop stopping bounds: `loop.Round.MaxRounds`, `loop.RoundLimitError`, `loop.Hooks.Progress`, `loop.NoProgressRounds` and `loop.NoProgressError`. A round ends only by a terminal call, a response without a tool call or an error; defaults are unchanged because zero `MaxRounds` and a nil `Progress` hook already meant neither stop was active. No setting or fixed bound replaces them.
- Remove the climb option levers: `DisableParallelToolCalls` on `provider.Request`, `loop.Request` and `loop.Round`; `provider.Request.AuthorityBoundary`; `InputBudgetBytes` on `loop.Direct` and `loop.FailOverBudget` (with `loop.MinInputBudgetBytes`); `tools.Tools.ResultBound` and `ResultHead` (with `tools.New`, `Tools.Validate` and `Tools.Cut`); and `tools.Documentation.ResultBound` and `BodyBound` (with `Documentation.Validate`). Behavior is fixed at the former defaults: a 524288-byte input window (smaller model-family bounds still apply), a 16384/4096 result cut, a 16384-byte documentation result and 8388608-byte response prefix, provider-default parallel calls and three default cache breakpoints. Defaults are unchanged; no setting replaces the removed options.
- Remove the per-call shell time limit `tools.Tools.ShellTimeout`, with its configured shell description and timed-out feedback. Shell calls behave as they did with the field unset: no per-call time limit, unchanged default definitions and result bytes, and cancellation and deadlines still stop loop-owned shell process groups. `Tools.Definition` remains and returns the default definitions; `sys.Options.Timeout` is unchanged. No setting replaces it.
- Stop every shell at the end of its run: shell calls forward their context (`sys.Session.RunContext`), so cancellation or a deadline covers a shell before, during and after startup and is joined before returning; each round ends the groups it started on success and ordinary failure too, keeping background processes alive only between its calls; and a killed host's supervisor completes whole-group SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL escalation, leaving a keeper for a group that outlives its shell. No option, per-call limit or timeout changes; groups started before the round and detached processes are untouched.
- Bind saved openai-compatible keys to the origin they were logged in at (L-CRED-ORIGIN): `openai-compatible.json` now holds `origin` beside `provider` and `api_key`; the key is sent only to a matching origin, a different origin or an unbound key fails before any request, and plain HTTP is allowed only keyless to localhost or a literal loopback IP. Add `Client.LoginWithBaseURL` (`Login` is unchanged and refuses openai-compatible without a URL). Existing compatible keys must be saved again. Other providers are unchanged.
- Confine caller-named reads to the root (L-READ-CONTAIN): `read_file`, `view_image` and the `path` of `list_files` and `search_text` refuse `~`, absolute paths outside `tools.Tools.Root`, parent escapes and symlinks that leave the root, with an `error:` result; reads inside the root, inside symlinks, a symlinked root and line ranges are unchanged. The four tool descriptions say so. No option is added; `write_file`, shell, probe, documentation and credential paths are unchanged.
- Preserve Responses outcomes and diagnostics (L-PROVIDER-PROTO): a refusal part is kept in the `round.ended` claim in content order with `output_text`, joined by a newline (the ending stays `no_call`); an effective Responses output with two function calls sharing a `call_id` is rejected whole as an invalid response, with the existing single retry, before any call is exposed or run; a failed or incomplete terminal envelope's identity and usage reach the failed attempt record under the existing nullable usage rules (a cut stream stays unknown); and attempt records now keep allowlisted `provider_failure` diagnostics for definite failures (with `incomplete_reason` for an incomplete response) and the bounded `validation` evidence of a discarded invalid completion, recovered retries included. No option, ending, exit code or normal-response byte changes.
- Preserve failed writes and report refusals (L-LOOP-CORRECT): `write_file` writes a same-directory temporary replacement, checks write and close, and renames it over the target only on success, so a failed write (for example a partial write ending in `efbig`) leaves the previous bytes intact and no temporary file; an existing symlink is followed and stays a link, existing permission bits are kept, nonregular targets and read-only files are refused without a change, and a hardlink alias keeps its preimage (the replacement is a new inode). A Responses `refusal` part is now part of `round.ended.claim`, joined with `output_text` parts by newline in the order received. `loop.Direct.Request` and `provider.Client.Respond` return `validation/missing_session: Session is required` for a nil Session instead of panicking, before any credential or transport use. No option is added; successful write bytes, tool results and provider requests are unchanged.
- Stop counting the ps listing as a group member on macOS (L-SYS-GROUPS-MAC): without `/proc`, the supervisor and keeper no longer count the `ps` process they start as a member of the group it lists, so an ended command's empty group is not left with a keeper and `sys.Session.LiveGroups` no longer reports it live; a group with a leftover member is still live. Linux and every option are unchanged.
- End provider attempts that make no progress (L-IDLE-STREAM): the per-attempt silence limits (90 s ChatGPT and 45 s other providers for the first progress, 180 s idle) are now renewed only by response progress, not by any body byte. On Responses and Messages a read is progress when it completes an SSE event with a `data:` field that is not a keep-alive (comment lines, blank lines and Messages `ping` events); on a body read whole (non-streaming Chat Completions and HTTP error bodies) the headers start the clock and a read renews it only with a byte other than JSON whitespace. A stream that sent progress and then only keep-alives now ends as a transient `idle` failure at the existing limit and is retried, instead of staying open until the 30-minute budget. Every attempt record gains `last_progress_ms` (null when no progress came) beside `last_byte_ms`. No limit value, option, timeout or retry change.
- Overlap independent streamed tool calls (L-TOOL-OVERLAP): without `AfterResponse`, `BeforeCall`, `HandleCall` or `AfterCall` hooks, `loop.Run` starts each complete streamed call (Responses `response.output_item.done`, Messages `content_block_stop`) before the response ends and runs independent calls concurrently: native reads with each other, writes to provably distinct files beside each other and unrelated reads. Same-file, aliased and read/write-overlapping calls stay ordered, and `shell`, `probe`, `documentation` and unknown calls are barriers against all others. Results and history keep the original call order, nothing is published until the validated response has all its results, and a failed attempt, tool stop, cancellation or deadline cancels and joins its calls first. Hooked rounds keep the serial order. No option, field, limit, timeout or retry change; Chat Completions and completed-response requesters dispatch after validation.
- Wait for Retry-After before provider retries (L-RETRY-AFTER): on every HTTP route, a retried 429 or 503 carrying a `Retry-After` header (RFC 9110 delay-seconds or HTTP-date) now waits exactly the advertised time instead of the fixed 2 s/8 s backoff, still bounded by the response budget and cancellation. An advertised wait above a fixed 60 s (inclusive bound) ends the call at once with `provider/unavailable` and the detail `<Label> asked to wait <N> s before retrying, more than the 60 s limit: <attempt detail>`. Without a usable header the 2 s/8 s schedule stays. The attempt count (3), the unreadable-answer retry, the 401 refresh, single-shot ChatGPT requests and request bytes are unchanged; no option is added.
- Continue runs within the request budget (L-REQUEST-BUDGET): `loop.Direct` condenses a request that exceeds the 524288-byte window (or a smaller family bound) instead of refusing it. Older complete exchanges and any earlier summary become a model-written summary message (same provider, role, credentials and transport, no tools, every request within the ceiling) beside the exact instructions, original task, user messages (a `Session`'s feedback to a terminal call included) and recent exchanges; calls and results are never separated. Condensation is bounded, stops honestly on provider failure, cancellation or inability to reduce, and an irreducible request is still refused with `context_budget_exceeded` before sending. A new `context.condensed` event discloses it, the summary stays in session history and `session.json`, `loop.Direct` gains the optional `Condensed` callback, and capabilities now report `compaction: true` and `context_policies: ["condense_over_budget"]`. The ceiling, reserve and output bounds are unchanged.
- Tell the agent to finish when its checks pass (L-STOP-AT-GREEN): `loop.DefaultInstructions` gains one final sentence, "When your checks pass, call finish right away: no extra re-reads, re-runs or polishing after a pass.", so a Session (and the CLI) with empty `instructions` sends it; the first four sentences, explicit task instructions, tool descriptions and every other model-facing text are byte-identical. Finish stays a claim and independent verification is unchanged. No command, flag, option or limit is added. Evidence (24 paired blocks: 12 Go tasks, two repetitions, gpt-6.1-terra high): with the sentence, wall time was lower in 21/24 (sign p=0.0003, ratio 0.83), cost ratio 0.79-0.83 and requests 0.78-0.80; all 48 runs passed the hidden graders in both arms. Two other candidate sentences (combined checks, write once) were tested in the same design and dropped: no repeatable gain. Reproduction pack: historical kogen-bench revision `880f9ec8ca7a9f176a6c808cefb7985794914e87`, `reproduce/loopnight-instruction-levers/README.md` (patch `patches/l3.diff`, sha256 95702947201907f9580bf335ff5b1a8cd0f4dc2aad5223d29e9f9b8f66b3764f).
